# 1 Samuel Chapter 24 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Book:** 1 Samuel | **Chapter:** 24

---

### Verse 1
- **EMET:** "And-it-was when-Saul returned from-after [the]-Philistines, and-they-told-him, saying, "Behold, David [is] in-[the]-wilderness of-En-gedi.""
- **LOGOS:** "And it came to pass, when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, that they told him, saying, "Behold, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.""
- **PNEUMA:** "After Saul returned from fighting the Philistines, he was told, "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 2
- **EMET:** "And-took Saul three-thousand chosen men from-all Israel, and-went to-seek David and-his-men upon-[the]-face of-[the]-rocks of-[the]-wild-goats."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel and went to seek David and his men upon the face of the Rocks of the Wild Goats."
- **PNEUMA:** "So Saul took three thousand of Israel's best soldiers and went to search for David and his men near the Crags of the Wild Goats."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 3
- **EMET:** "And-he-came to-[the]-sheepfolds of-the-flock upon the-way, and-there [was]-a-cave, and-Saul went-in to-cover his-feet [le-hasekh et raglav]. And-David..."
- **LOGOS:** "And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, and there was a cave there. And Saul went in to cover his feet. Now David and his men were sitting in the in..."
- **PNEUMA:** "He came to some sheepfolds along the road where there was a cave. Saul went inside to relieve himself — not knowing that David and his men were hiding..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 4
- **EMET:** "And-said [the]-men of-David to-him, "Behold, the-day of-which YHWH said to-you, 'Behold, I [am]-giving your-enemy into-your-hand, and-you-shall-do to-..."
- **LOGOS:** "And the men of David said to him, "Behold, the day of which the LORD said to you, 'Behold, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to ..."
- **PNEUMA:** "David's men whispered, "This is the day the LORD told you about — 'I will hand your enemy over to you to do with as you wish.'" David crept forward an..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 5
- **EMET:** "And-it-was afterward, and-struck the-heart of-David him, because he-had-cut the-corner which [was]-to-Saul."
- **LOGOS:** "And it came to pass afterward that the heart of David struck him, because he had cut off the corner that belonged to Saul."
- **PNEUMA:** "But immediately his conscience stung him for what he had done."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 6
- **EMET:** "And-he-said to-his-men, "Far-be-it for-me from-YHWH if I-should-do this thing to-my-lord, to-[the]-anointed of-YHWH [meshiach YHWH], to-stretch-out my..."
- **LOGOS:** "And he said to his men, "Far be it from me, by the LORD, that I should do this thing to my lord, to the anointed of the LORD, to stretch out my hand a..."
- **PNEUMA:** "He told his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do anything to my master. He is the LORD's anointed — I will not raise my hand against him.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 7
- **EMET:** "And-David restrained [va-yeshassa'] his-men with-[these]-words and-did-not permit-them to-rise against-Saul. And-Saul arose from-the-cave and-went on-..."
- **LOGOS:** "And David restrained his men with these words and did not permit them to rise against Saul. And Saul arose from the cave and went on his way."
- **PNEUMA:** "With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. Saul got up, left the cave, and went on his way."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 8
- **EMET:** "And-arose David after-this and-went-out from-the-cave and-called after Saul, saying, "My-lord the-king!" And-looked Saul behind-him, and-bowed David [..."
- **LOGOS:** "And afterward David arose and went out of the cave, and he called after Saul, saying, "My lord the king!" And when Saul looked behind him, David bowed..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Then David came out of the cave and called after him, "My lord the king!" Saul turned around, and David bowed facedown to the ground."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 9
- **EMET:** "And-said David to-Saul, "Why do-you-listen to-[the]-words of-a-man, saying, 'Behold, David seeks your-harm'?"
- **LOGOS:** "And David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of men who say, 'Behold, David seeks to harm you'?"
- **PNEUMA:** "David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to people who say I'm trying to harm you?"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 10
- **EMET:** "Behold, this day your-eyes have-seen that YHWH gave-you today into-my-hand in-the-cave, and-[someone]-said to-kill-you, but-I-spared-you [va-tachas]. ..."
- **LOGOS:** "Behold, this day your eyes have seen that the LORD gave you today into my hand in the cave. And someone said to kill you, but my eye spared you. And I..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Today you can see with your own eyes that the LORD put you in my power in that cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not ra..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 11
- **EMET:** "And-my-father, see, indeed see the-corner of-your-robe in-my-hand, for when-I-cut the-corner of-your-robe, I-did-not kill-you. Know and-see that there..."
- **LOGOS:** "And my father, see — yes, see the corner of your robe in my hand! For in that I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you, know and see tha..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Look, my father — look at this piece of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe but did not kill you. Doesn't this prove there is no t..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 12
- **EMET:** "May-YHWH judge between-me and-between-you, and-may-YHWH avenge-me from-you, but-my-hand shall-not be against-you."
- **LOGOS:** "May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me against you, but my hand shall not be against you."
- **PNEUMA:** "May the LORD judge between us. May the LORD vindicate me against you — but my hand will never touch you."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 13
- **EMET:** "As-says the-proverb [mashal] of-the-ancients, 'From-the-wicked goes-out wickedness,' but-my-hand shall-not be against-you."
- **LOGOS:** "As the proverb of the ancients says, 'From the wicked comes forth wickedness,' but my hand shall not be against you."
- **PNEUMA:** "As the old proverb says, 'From wicked people comes wickedness' — but my hand will never touch you."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 14
- **EMET:** "After whom has-the-king of-Israel gone-out? After whom are-you-pursuing? After a-dead dog, after a-single flea?"
- **LOGOS:** "After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog! After a single flea!"
- **PNEUMA:** "Who is the king of Israel chasing? A dead dog? A single flea?"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 16
- **EMET:** "And-it-was when-David-finished speaking these words to-Saul, and-said Saul, "Is-this your-voice, my-son David?" And-Saul lifted-up his-voice and-wept."
- **LOGOS:** "And it came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And Saul lifted up his ..."
- **PNEUMA:** "When David finished speaking, Saul said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" And Saul broke down and wept."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 17
- **EMET:** "And-he-said to-David, "You [are]-more-righteous than-I, for you have-repaid-me the-good, and-I have-repaid-you the-evil."
- **LOGOS:** "And he said to David, "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good, whereas I have repaid you with evil."
- **PNEUMA:** ""You are a better man than I am," he said. "You have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 18
- **EMET:** "And-you have-declared today that you-have-done good with-me, in-that YHWH delivered-me into-your-hand and-you-did-not kill-me."
- **LOGOS:** "And you have declared today that you have done good to me, in that the LORD delivered me into your hand and you did not kill me."
- **PNEUMA:** "Today you have shown how well you have treated me — the LORD delivered me into your hands and you did not kill me."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 19
- **EMET:** "For if a-man finds his-enemy, will-he-send-him-away on-[a]-good way? And-YHWH shall-repay-you good in-place-of this day which you-have-done for-me."
- **LOGOS:** "For if a man finds his enemy, will he send him away on a good path? May the LORD repay you with good for what you have done for me this day."
- **PNEUMA:** "What man, finding his enemy, lets him walk away unharmed? May the LORD reward you for what you have done for me today."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 21
- **EMET:** "And-now swear to-me by-YHWH that you-will-not cut-off my-seed after-me and-that you-will-not destroy my-name from-[the]-house of-my-father.""
- **LOGOS:** "Swear to me now by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me, and that you will not destroy my name from the house of my father.""
- **PNEUMA:** "Now swear to me by the LORD that you will not wipe out my descendants and that you will not erase my family name.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 22
- **EMET:** "And-swore David to-Saul. And-went Saul to-his-house, and-David and-his-men went-up to-the-stronghold."
- **LOGOS:** "And David swore to Saul. And Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up to the stronghold."
- **PNEUMA:** "David gave Saul his oath. Then Saul went home, and David and his men returned to the stronghold."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.

— SOPHIA
